correctness.rationale: For the finite level-m triangle-based Sierpinski gasket, the three-corner inverse Green function splits into 1 symmetric and 2 standard sectors. Old-vertex Schur complement gives rational recursion k_(m+1)(z)=((z+2)k_m(z(z-3))+2z)/((z+1)(z-2)), with bases z-2 and z+1. Reduced denominators and evaluations at -2,4,10 control cancellations; numerator-degree recurrences give a_m=2^(m-1)+1 and b_m=2^m for m>=1. The spectral theorem counts corner-active ranks a+2b=5*2^(m-1)+1 (rank 3 at m0). A corner-supported Hermitian perturbation and nonzero hopping preserve the cyclic subspace, and positive jump rates remove precisely its complement; maximally mixed capture =rank/N. Independent modular Krylov ranks for m0..4 matched, distinct from all-generation proof.

originality.rationale: Prior graph-Laplacian formulation H=4I-A-2BB* is equivalent as to accessible corner subspace. Previously reported dark dimensions for sizes up to 366 coincide with finite instances of the formula; those finite cases are credited, not re-claimed. Schur-complement recurrence and coprimality analysis are necessary to extend finite tabulations. The general reduced-Krylov theorem plus a tabulated dimension is insufficient to force the exact rank formula for all m. Best-of-knowledge priority risk remains explicit; unsuccessful search alone is not claimed as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Fractal spectral-decimation tables or boundary Green functions in older specialist papers may imply the same rank without transport language.
The result presumes strictly positive absorption at all three corners, uniform interior hopping and a maximally mixed initial state; it does not imply all initial states are fully captured.
